tagline: Turn emails into Slack messages and vice versa automatically
metaTitle: Gmail + Slack Integration: VIP Emails to Slack Channels
metaDescription: Route VIP emails to the right Slack channels and get a daily inbox digest there. GAIA also turns Slack decisions into email drafts. See the setup steps.
intro:
Most teams live inside two communication tools every day, yet Gmail and Slack operate in completely separate silos. Important client emails sit unread while the team is active in chat. Urgent chat messages get missed because a colleague is heads-down in their inbox. The result is duplicated effort, missed context, and a constant scramble to keep both channels synchronized.

GAIA bridges the two so information flows between inbox and chat automatically. When a high-priority email arrives, GAIA can route it to the relevant Slack channel with full context. When a decision is made in a thread, GAIA can draft a follow-up email and queue it for review. Instead of manually translating between two communication platforms, your team gets a unified workflow where email and chat reinforce each other.

This integration is especially powerful for customer-facing teams who receive client emails but collaborate internally in chat, and for operations teams who need to loop in colleagues on important vendor communications without forwarding chains that lose context.

useCases.title: Route VIP emails to Slack channels
useCases.description: GAIA monitors the inbox for emails from key clients, executives, or priority senders and posts a formatted summary to the designated channel so the right people are notified.

useCases.title: Convert Slack decisions into email drafts
useCases.description: When a decision is finalized in a thread, ask GAIA to draft the corresponding client email. It reads the thread context and composes a professional reply ready for your review in Gmail.

useCases.title: Daily digest by direct message
useCases.description: GAIA compiles a morning digest of your most important unread emails and posts a structured summary to your personal Slack DM so you start each day knowing exactly what needs attention.

useCases.title: Support ticket escalation
useCases.description: Customer support emails that exceed response SLAs trigger an automatic alert in your support channel, including the sender, subject, and time since receipt so nothing slips through.

useCases.title: Meeting confirmation sync
useCases.description: When a meeting confirmation lands in the inbox, GAIA posts a heads-up to the relevant channel so everyone knows the meeting is confirmed without requiring a manual announcement.

howItWorks.step: Connect Gmail and Slack to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authenticate your Gmail account and Slack workspace in GAIA's integration settings. Both connections use OAuth so your credentials stay secure and GAIA only accesses what it needs.
Tell GAIA which emails should route to which channels, what format the notifications should take, and when you want digests delivered. You can use natural language to describe the rules.
Once configured, GAIA monitors the inbox continuously and executes your rules without you lifting a finger. You can adjust rules anytime by simply telling GAIA what you want changed.

faqs.question: Can GAIA post entire emails to a channel or just summaries?
faqs.answer: Both. GAIA can post the full email body, a concise AI-generated summary, or just the key metadata (sender, subject, time) depending on what you specify. For long emails, summaries are usually more practical in a channel.

faqs.question: Will GAIA send emails from Slack automatically or always ask me first?
faqs.answer: By default GAIA drafts emails for your review before sending. You can configure it to auto-send for specific low-stakes scenarios like meeting confirmations, but GAIA will always respect your preference for human approval on outbound communications.

faqs.question: Does this work with Gmail labels and channels together?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can instruct GAIA to monitor specific labels and route them to corresponding channels. For example, emails labeled 'Urgent' can go to a #urgent channel while emails labeled 'Newsletters' are silently archived.
